input.title: Vetra remote drives enable collaborative development by syncing document models across team members via ph init/checkout/vetra commands

input.description: ph init --remote-drive creates projects connected to shared drives; ph checkout clones existing projects; ph vetra starts dev environment.

input.content: Vetra remote drives enable team collaboration: `ph init --remote-drive <url>` creates a new project connected to a remote Vetra drive, adding `vetra.driveId` and `vetra.driveUrl` to `powerhouse.config.json`. `ph checkout --remote-drive <url>` clones an existing project by querying the remote drive for its configured GitHub URL. `ph vetra` starts Switchboard connected to the remote drive with auto-sync and Connect Studio. The `--watch` flag creates a second 'Vetra Preview' drive for testing local changes while the main drive stays stable. The preview drive dynamically loads local document models and editors. Key distinction: without remote drive, `ph vetra` creates a local drive only; with remote drive, it syncs across team members.

Vetra remote drives enable team collaboration: `ph init --remote-drive <url>` (short form `-r`) creates a new project connected to a remote Vetra drive, adding `vetra.driveId` and `vetra.driveUrl` to `powerhouse.config.json` — `driveId` is just the last path segment of the URL. `ph vetra` then starts Switchboard connected to the remote drive with auto-sync and Connect Studio; you do not have to re-pass the URL, because `ph vetra`'s own `--remote-drive` option has a `defaultValue` that reads `getConfig().vetra?.driveUrl`. The `--watch` / `-w` flag creates a second 'Vetra Preview' drive for testing local changes while the main drive stays stable (`// Add preview drive (only in watch mode)`); the preview drive dynamically loads local document models and editors. Key distinction: without a remote drive, `ph vetra` runs against a local Vetra Switchboard drive only; with a remote drive, it syncs across team members.

**`ph checkout` is legacy and unreachable — do not teach it.** The command survives only as `clis/ph-cmd/legacy/commands/checkout.ts` and is registered in neither `phCliCommandNames` (`packages/shared/clis/command-names.ts`) nor the `ph` entrypoint's cmd-ts tree (`clis/ph-cmd/src/commands/ph.ts`, whose subcommands are exactly `init`, `use`, `update`, `setup-globals`, `use-local` plus the help commands). It is not even shipped: `tsdown.config.ts` builds only `src/cli.ts`, `package.json` publishes only `dist`, and `tsconfig.json` has `"exclude": [..., "legacy"]`. That exclusion is load-bearing — the file would not compile if it were built, because it imports `../utils/package-manager.js`, which does not exist. The generated `clis/ph-cmd/COMMANDS.md` lists only Init, Use, Update, Setup Globals and Use Local, confirming it is out of the live tree. The academy still teaches it in five places across two pages (`04-Reference/07-CLITooling/06-VetraRemoteDrive.md` and `05-Lookup/00-Cookbook.md`), and `COMMANDS-LEGACY.md` documents it too. All of that is stale.

What it *did*, for context: derive the drive id from the URL, query the drive's Vetra package document over GraphQL for a `githubUrl`, `git clone` that repo, then run the package manager's `install`. Note that it never wrote any config — the cloned repo's committed `powerhouse.config.json` already carried the `vetra` block.

**Joining an existing remote-drive project today.** There is no supported single command; this is a genuine gap, not a renamed flag. `ph init --remote-drive` is built to *create* a project bound to a drive, and it explicitly does not want an already-initialized one. The manual equivalent is:

```bash
git clone <githubUrl>        # obtained out of band; checkout used to auto-discover this from the drive
cd <repo> && pnpm install
ph vetra                     # --remote-drive defaults to config vetra.driveUrl
```

This works only because the committed `powerhouse.config.json` already contains `vetra.driveUrl`. If it does not, you must hand-edit the file to add `"vetra": { "driveId": "...", "driveUrl": "..." }` or pass `ph vetra --remote-drive <url>` on every invocation — there is no `setConfig` helper for this key. The only writers of the `vetra` block are the two codegen scaffold paths (`packages/codegen/src/templates/boilerplate/powerhouse.config.json.ts` and `packages/codegen/src/file-builders/boilerplate/generated-project-files.ts`), i.e. **the block can only be produced at `ph init` time**. Also worth knowing: `vetra.driveId` is written but never read back by either CLI; only `driveUrl` is consumed.

**Live trap.** `clis/ph-cli/src/utils/validate-remote-drive.ts` still prints, on the exact scenario above, "please use the checkout command instead: ph checkout --remote-drive <remote drive url>" — pointing users at the dead command. Worse, it returns `false` and `clis/ph-cli/src/services/init.ts` ignores the return value, so pointing `ph init --remote-drive` at an existing project's drive prints a red ❌, then a green "✅ Remote drive set up.", then scaffolds a brand-new project anyway.

Verified in `packages/shared/clis/{command-names.ts,args/{init,vetra}.ts,types.ts,file-system/get-config.ts}`, `clis/ph-cmd/src/{cli.ts,commands/ph.ts}`, `clis/ph-cli/src/{services/{init,vetra}.ts,utils/validate-remote-drive.ts}` and the two codegen writers at 6.2.2-dev.45.

_Source-verified 2026-08-13 against Powerhouse source at v6.2.2-dev.45._

input.title: Vetra remote drives enable collaborative development via ph init --remote-drive and ph vetra; ph checkout is legacy and unregistered

input.description: ph init --remote-drive creates projects connected to shared drives and writes the vetra config block; ph vetra reads it back. ph checkout is dead — joining an existing project is manual.
